'''Benjamin Michael McAdams''' (born December 5, 1974) is an American politician and attorney who is the [[United States House of Representatives|United States representative-elect]] from [[Utah's 1st congressional district|Utah's 1st congressional district.]] He previously served as the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] from [[Utah's 4th congressional district]] from 2019 to 2021. McAdams was the Democratic nominee for [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 1|Utah's 1st congressional district]] for the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah|2026 election]], defeating Republican nominee Riley Owen.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Gehrke |first1=Robert |last2=Jayswal |first2=Palak |last3=Nov. 3 |first3=Isabel Meléndez-Rivera {{!}} |last4=2026 |last5=Nov. 4 |first5=8:00 p m {{!}} Updated |last6=2026 |last7=A.m |first7=10:12 |title=I'm 'going to fight' for Utahns, Ben McAdams vows, as Democrats win a seat in Congress |url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2026/11/03/mcadams-favored-win-congressional/ |access-date=2026-11-05 |website=The Salt Lake Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

From 2013 to 2019, he served as mayor of [[Salt Lake County, Utah|Salt Lake County]], and from 2009 to 2012, he was the [[Utah State Senate|Utah state senator]] from the [[2nd Utah Senate District|2nd district]], which includes [[Salt Lake City]], [[South Salt Lake]], and a portion of [[West Valley, Utah|West Valley]].<ref name="UtahLawProfile">[https://faculty.utah.edu/u0075058-BENJAMIN_MICHAEL_MCADAMS/biography/index.hml Benjamin Michael Adams: Volunteer Faculty] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201215035912/https://faculty.utah.edu/u0075058-BENJAMIN_MICHAEL_MCADAMS/hm/index.hml |date=December 15, 2020 }}, [[University of Utah College of Law]]</ref> McAdams was elected to Congress in [[2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 4|2018]], narrowly defeating two-term Republican incumbent [[Mia Love]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/11/20/its-over-democrat-ben/|title=It's over. Democrat Ben McAdams ousts Republican Rep Mia Love by 694 votes|publisher=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|author=Lee Davidson|date=November 20, 2018|access-date=November 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201211123651/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/11/20/its-over-democrat-ben/|archive-date=December 11, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |date=November 20, 2018 |title=It's Congressman-elect Ben McAdams after election results certified, but Love hasn't conceded |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/46431630/its-congressman-elect-ben-mcadams-after-election-results-certified |access-date=November 20, 2018 |publisher=KSL.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926092309/https://www.ksl.com/article/46431630/its-congressman-elect-ben-mcadams-after-election-results-certified |archive-date=September 26, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref><!-- author line says "By Lisa Riley Roche, Deseret News"  --> In [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 4|2020]], McAdams ran for reelection, but he lost to Republican challenger [[Burgess Owens]].<ref name="2020election">{{Cite news |date=2020-11-16 |title=McAdams concedes Utah's 4th Congressional District race to Owens |language=en |work=KSTU |url=https://www.fox13now.com/news/election-2020/mcadams-concedes-utahs-4th-congressional-district-race-to-owens |access-date=2020-11-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116232123/https://www.fox13now.com/news/election-2020/mcadams-concedes-utahs-4th-congressional-district-race-to-owens |archive-date=November 16, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> He is the most recent Democrat to represent Utah in Congress, and during his tenure, was the only [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] member of Utah's congressional delegation.

==Early life and education==
McAdams was born in [[West Bountiful, Utah]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=52903075&itype=CMSID|title=State Sen. McAdams to run for S.L. County mayor|publisher=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=November 16, 2011|author=Robert Gehrke|access-date=November 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404015750/https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=52903075&itype=CMSID|archive-date=April 4, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He has a bachelor's degree in political science from the [[University of Utah]] and a J.D. with honors from [[Columbia Law School]].<ref name="UtahLawProfile"/><ref name="McAdamsProfile Deseret">{{cite web|last1=Roche|first1=Lisa Riley|title=New Utah state senator Ben McAdams is youthful but not naive|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705360440/New-Utah-state-senator-Ben-McAdams-is-youthful-but-not-naive.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210082714/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705360440/New-Utah-state-senator-Ben-McAdams-is-youthful-but-not-naive.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 10, 2015|newspaper=Deseret News|access-date=February 9, 2015|date=January 23, 2010}}</ref> At Columbia, McAdams was a member of the ''[[Columbia Human Rights Law Review]]''.<ref name="UtahLawProfile"/>

==Early career==

=== Legal career ===
After graduating from law school, McAdams briefly worked in New York City as an associate at the law firm [[Davis Polk & Wardwell]].<ref name="UtahLawProfile"/><ref name="McAdamsProfile Deseret"/> McAdams and his family then returned to Utah,<ref name="McAdamsProfile Deseret"/> where he joined the law firm Dorsey & Whitney in [[Salt Lake City]], working in [[securities law]].<ref name="UtahLawProfile"/> McAdams then became Senior Advisor to [[Mayor of Salt Lake City|Salt Lake City Mayor]] [[Ralph Becker (mayor)|Ralph Becker]].<ref name="UtahLawProfile"/>

McAdams has served as an adjunct faculty member at the [[University of Utah College of Law]].<ref name="UtahLawProfile"/>

===Utah state senator===
McAdams was elected to replace [[Scott McCoy]] as the senator for Utah's second district in a special election on December 19, 2009.<ref>"Democrats tap McAdams for Seat in Legislature"</ref> He was elected to a four-year term on November 2, 2010.

====Legislation====

In March 2011, McAdams proposed a bill banning employment and housing discrimination against gay and transgender [[Utah]]ns. His attempt to advance the bill failed on a party-line vote. At the time, he stated the ideas in the bill had “proven to be a success” in cities that had adopted similar measures.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/19111246/committee-halts-bill-combating-discrimination-of-lgbt-communities|title=Committee halts bill combating discrimination of LGBT communities|publisher = KSL.com|date=February 3, 2012|access-date=March 15, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=51331829&itype=CMSID | author=Robert Gehrke | title=Senate: No hearing for anti-discrimination bill | newspaper=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] | date=February 28, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404015743/https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=51331829&itype=CMSID | archive-date=April 4, 2019 | access-date=February 19, 2018 | url-status=live}}</ref> Salt Lake City passed a similar measure in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldextra.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/legislature/senator-introducing-statewide-nondiscrimination-bill/article_eda9226d-a06e-581a-abfd-1e03fd61c6cd.html|publisher=Daily Herald|title=Senator introducing statewide nondiscrimination bill|access-date=September 15, 2018|archive-date=March 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329011332/https://www.heraldextra.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/legislature/senator-introducing-statewide-nondiscrimination-bill/article_eda9226d-a06e-581a-abfd-1e03fd61c6cd.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Mayoralty (2013-2019) ===

[[File:L-15-01-30-A-295 (16401290016).jpg|thumb|250px|alt=Salt Lake County Mayor Ben McAdams and U.S. Secretary of Labor Tom Perez visit Palmer Court, the Road Home's permanent supportive housing development, in Salt Lake City, Utah, on Friday, January 30, 2015.|upright=1.3|McAdams and [[Secretary of Labor]] [[Tom Perez]] in Salt Lake City on January 30, 2015]]

====Elections====

In November 2011, McAdams announced his campaign to succeed [[Peter Corroon]] as [[mayor]] of [[Salt Lake County, Utah]].<ref>"State Sen. Ben McAdams officially enters race for Salt Lake County mayor"</ref> McAdams was elected, on November 6, 2012, defeating Republican nominee Mark Crockett 54% to 45%.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/politics/55201789-90/county-mcadams-crockett-mayor.html.csp | title = Ben McAdams wins Salt Lake County mayor's race | publisher = Salt Lake Tribune | access-date = November 13, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170107182327/http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/politics/55201789-90/county-mcadams-crockett-mayor.html.csp | archive-date = January 7, 2017 | url-status = live}}</ref> McAdams resigned from the state senate before taking office as mayor.

McAdams was mentioned as a potential candidate in Utah's [[United States Senate election in Utah, 2016|2016 Senate race]] or Utah's [[Utah gubernatorial election, 2016|2016 gubernatorial race]], but did not run for either position.<ref>{{cite web |last=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |date=April 8, 2015 |title=Poll: Josh Romney would be a tough opponent for Sen. Mike Lee |url=https://www.deseret.com/2015/4/9/20562294/poll-josh-romney-would-be-a-tough-opponent-for-sen-mike-lee/ |access-date=August 19, 2015 |work=[[Deseret News]]}}</ref><ref name=16in16>{{cite web|url=http://www.politico.com/story/2014/12/2016-senate-races-113837_Page4.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231184744/http://www.politico.com/story/2014/12/2016-senate-races-113837_Page4.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 31, 2014|title=16 in '16: The new battle for the Senate|date=December 29, 2014|access-date=December 29, 2014|work=[[Politico]]|last=Cheney|first=Kyle}}</ref> He was reelected to a second term as Salt Lake County Mayor in November 2016 59% to 41%.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://slco.org/clerk/electionsEK/results/results_arch/2016General.html|title=Official Election Results 2016 General Election|work=Salt Lake County|date=November 22, 2016|access-date=December 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928065040/https://slco.org/clerk/electionsEK/results/results_arch/2016General.html|archive-date=September 28, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Homelessness====
{{See also|Homelessness in the United States by state#Utah}}

McAdams was tasked by the Utah Legislature to select a location for a new homeless shelter in Salt Lake County, outside of Salt Lake City. According to the [[Deseret News]], the task was considered politically damaging,<ref name="DeseretHomeless">{{cite news |last=McKellar |first=Katie |date=February 13, 2018 |title=Salt Lake County Mayor Ben McAdams renews pledge to pull support of homeless site if revenue bill fails |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900010260/salt-lake-mayor-ben-mcadams-renews-pledge-to-nix-homeless-site-if-revenue-bill-fails.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180214194647/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900010260/salt-lake-mayor-ben-mcadams-renews-pledge-to-nix-homeless-site-if-revenue-bill-fails.html |archive-date=February 14, 2018 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> as strong local opposition was expected regardless of the ultimate shelter location. McAdams recommended [[South Salt Lake, Utah|South Salt Lake]], and was opposed by Cherie Wood, the city's mayor.<ref>{{cite news |last=McKellar |first=Katie |date=March 31, 2017 |title=Mayor calls plan for homeless shelter a 'lethal blow' for South Salt Lake <!--check? better archive link might be https://web.archive.org/web/20170402192605/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865676819/County-chooses-South-Salt-Lake-for-new-homeless-resource-center.html --> |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865676819/County-chooses-South-Salt-Lake-for-new-homeless-resource-center.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331184808/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865676819/County-chooses-South-Salt-Lake-for-new-homeless-resource-center.html |archive-date=March 31, 2017 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> Previously, [[Draper, UT|Draper]] mayor Troy Walker had volunteered two sites for the shelter in Draper, before rescinding the offer under public pressure.<ref>{{cite news |last=McKellar |first=Katie |title='I get it now': Draper mayor rescinds homeless sites offer during raucous public gathering |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865676709/I-dont-think-we-can-do-it-Draper-mayor-rescinds-homeless-sites-offer-during-raucous-public.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330063146/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865676709/I-dont-think-we-can-do-it-Draper-mayor-rescinds-homeless-sites-offer-during-raucous-public.html |archive-date=March 30, 2017 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref>

Before making his recommendation, McAdams spent two nights on the streets of Salt Lake City, posing as a homeless person to gather information.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2017/08/06/sl-co-mayor-ben-mcadams-posed-as-a-homeless-person-for-3-days-and-2-nights-heres-what-he-saw/|title=Mayor Ben McAdams posed as a homeless person for 3 days and 2 nights. Here's what he saw.|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=August 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181127222352/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2017/08/06/sl-co-mayor-ben-mcadams-posed-as-a-homeless-person-for-3-days-and-2-nights-heres-what-he-saw/|archive-date=November 27, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=McKellar |first=Katie |date=August 6, 2017 |title='I didn't feel safe': Mayor Ben McAdams describes secret nights on street, in shelter |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865686230/I-didnt-feel-safe-Mayor-Ben-McAdams-describes-secret-nights-on-street-in-shelter.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806095610/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865686230/I-didnt-feel-safe-Mayor-Ben-McAdams-describes-secret-nights-on-street-in-shelter.html |archive-date=August 6, 2017 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> Although tasked with recommending a site for the shelter, McAdams pledged to not support the center's groundbreaking unless the Utah Legislature passes a bill to create a pool of revenue from other cities to help with funding.<ref name="DeseretHomeless"/>

McAdams has called for a "radically different approach ... to address homelessness", and has called homelessness a "stubborn and complex social challenge".<ref name="DeseretHomeless"/>

====Taxes and budgets====

In 2014, McAdams supported the renewal of a Zoos, Arts, and Parks (ZAP) tax in Salt Lake County.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/32145598/parks-and-recreation--zap-tax-on-the-2014-ballot|title=ZAP tax on the 2014 ballot|publisher=ksl.com|author=Sara Jarman|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=October 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404004046/https://www.ksl.com/article/32145598/parks-and-recreation--zap-tax-on-the-2014-ballot|archive-date=April 4, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> The ZAP tax amounts to 1 cent on every $10 spent. It partially funds more than 190 county arts and cultural organizations, as well as 30 parks and recreation facilities, including [[Hogle Zoo]], [[Tracy Aviary]], the [[Loveland Living Planet Aquarium]], and others. The tax was approved by voters in 2014, with nearly 77% of county voters in favor.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/2017/12/28/20637594/s-l-county-oks-zap-tax-funding-for-25-organizations/|title=S.L. County OKs ZAP tax funding for 25 organizations|date=December 28, 2017|publisher=Deseret News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812015349/https://www.deseret.com/2017/12/28/20637594/s-l-county-oks-zap-tax-funding-for-25-organizations/|archive-date=August 12, 2025|access-date=November 7, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Economic and community development====

McAdams supported a Utah bill that gave Salt Lake County's townships the power to decide their future governance structure. This led to the election in which [[Millcreek, UT|Millcreek]] residents voted to incorporate.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cortez |first=Marjorie |title=Community preservation bill creates governance options for Salt Lake County |url=https://www.deseret.com/2015/3/13/20560690/community-preservation-bill-creates-governance-options-for-salt-lake-county/ |publisher=Deseret News |publication-date=March 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812015431/https://www.deseret.com/2015/3/13/20560690/community-preservation-bill-creates-governance-options-for-salt-lake-county/ |archive-date=August 12, 2025 |access-date=November 7, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=3133985&itype=CMSID|title=Millcreek to become Salt Lake County's 17th city|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181230030404/http://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=3133985&itype=CMSID|archive-date=December 30, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

McAdams opposed a proposed [[Facebook]] data center in [[West Jordan, UT|West Jordan]] in 2016. West Jordan city leaders blamed opposition from Salt Lake County, and McAdams in particular, for Facebook's ultimate choice to locate the data center in [[New Mexico]] instead of West Jordan. The $2.5 billion data center would have received $195 million from the city and county in tax breaks. McAdams believed that the data center was too expensive, since it would have directly produced a maximum of only 130 jobs. Supporters of the data center argued it would have drawn additional development and investment to the region.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=4352467&itype=CMSID|title=West Jordan blames Ben McAdams for losing out on Facebook data center|date=September 25, 2016|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=October 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010095529/http://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=4352467&itype=CMSID|archive-date=October 10, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Salt Lake County maintained an AAA bond rating throughout McAdams's tenure as mayor.<ref name="BittersweetGoodbye">{{cite web |last=McKellar |first=Katie |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Ben McAdams says 'bittersweet' goodbye to Salt Lake County mayor's office |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900048349/ben-mcadams-says-bittersweet-goodbye-to-salt-lake-county-mayors-office.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229043655/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900048349/ben-mcadams-says-bittersweet-goodbye-to-salt-lake-county-mayors-office.html |archive-date=December 29, 2018 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref>

==United States Representative==

===Elections===

==== 2018 ====
{{See also|2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 4}}

On October 18, 2017, McAdams announced that he would seek the Democratic nomination to oppose incumbent Representative [[Mia Love]], a Republican representing [[Utah's 4th congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ksl.com/?sid=46182704&nid=148&title=salt-lake-county-mayor-ben-mcadams-running-for-congress|title=Salt Lake County Mayor Ben McAdams running for Congress {{!}} KSL.com|access-date=October 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808012358/https://www.ksl.com/?sid=46182704&nid=148&title=salt-lake-county-mayor-ben-mcadams-running-for-congress|archive-date=August 8, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> On April 28, 2018, McAdams won the Democratic nomination at the party's convention. With the backing of 72% of the convention delegates, McAdams avoided a primary campaign.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/utah/articles/2018-04-28/utah-democrats-gather-to-select-congressional-nominees|title=Utah Democrats Nominate McAdams for House Race Against Love|publisher=U.S. News|date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809090902/https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/utah/articles/2018-04-28/utah-democrats-gather-to-select-congressional-nominees|archive-date=August 9, 2018|access-date=August 9, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Under pressure from Love’s campaign, McAdams stated that he would not support [[Nancy Pelosi]] for Speaker if elected.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/05/03/mcadams-would-vote-no-on-a-speaker-pelosi-love-campaign-says-if-dems-win-so-does-pelosi/|title=Love campaign says if Dems win, so does Pelosi, but McAdams says he wouldn't support the minority leader|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=August 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404003923/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/05/03/mcadams-would-vote-no-on-a-speaker-pelosi-love-campaign-says-if-dems-win-so-does-pelosi/|archive-date=April 4, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/democrats-opposing-pelosi-n899536|title=Democrats opposing Pelosi|date=August 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030094712/https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/democrats-opposing-pelosi-n899536|archive-date=October 30, 2019|access-date=October 11, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/utah/articles/2018-05-03/democrat-mcadams-wont-support-pelosi-for-speaker|title=Democrat McAdams Won't Support Pelosi for Speaker|date=May 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190217221413/https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/utah/articles/2018-05-03/democrat-mcadams-wont-support-pelosi-for-speaker|archive-date=February 17, 2019|access-date=October 11, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2018, CNN reported that the race was considered "consequential to both parties" because Love had "stood up to <nowiki>[President Donald Trump]</nowiki> on immigration" and "because national Democrats [saw] McAdams as one of their best chances to gain a foothold on red turf".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/29/politics/mia-love-ben-mcadams-utah/index.html|title=Utah's real race to watch isn't Mitt Romney's – it's Mia Love's|author=Maeve Reston|website=CNN|date=June 29, 2018|access-date=August 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190411214902/https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/29/politics/mia-love-ben-mcadams-utah/index.html|archive-date=April 11, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

McAdams was endorsed by the [[Blue Dog Coalition]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bluedogdems.com/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808043210/https://bluedogdems.com/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 8, 2018|title=Archive of bluedogdems.com|date=August 8, 2018}}</ref> a House caucus of conservative and moderate Democrats that stresses fiscal responsibility. He was also endorsed by the [[League of Conservation Voters]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://origin.lcv.org/article/lcv-action-fund-endorses-ben-mcadams-congress/|title=LCV Action Fund Endorses Ben McAdams for Congress|date=June 15, 2018|access-date=August 7, 2018|archive-date=February 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204172442/http://origin.lcv.org/article/lcv-action-fund-endorses-ben-mcadams-congress/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 20, final results showed that McAdams had won by 694 votes, or .257%. His margin of victory was greater than the .25% needed to automatically trigger a recount.<ref name=nov20>{{cite web|url=https://fox13now.com/2018/11/20/final-votes-in-salt-lake-utah-counties-tallied-mcadams-in-the-lead-over-mia-love/|title=Final votes counted in Salt Lake, Utah counties; McAdams victory holds|date=November 20, 2018|publisher=Fox13|author=Taylor Hartman|access-date=November 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404003854/https://fox13now.com/2018/11/20/final-votes-in-salt-lake-utah-counties-tallied-mcadams-in-the-lead-over-mia-love/|archive-date=April 4, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> About $11.4 million combined was spent by Love's and McAdams' campaigns, and outside groups on their behalf, making it one of the most expensive campaigns in Utah history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kutv.com/news/local/mcadams-vs-love-race-was-one-of-the-most-expensive-in-utah-history|title=McAdams vs. Love race was one of the most expensive in Utah history|author=BRADY McCOMBS|agency=Associated Press|date=December 7, 2018|website=KUTV|access-date=July 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709051128/https://kutv.com/news/local/mcadams-vs-love-race-was-one-of-the-most-expensive-in-utah-history|archive-date=July 9, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/0ff703c6668a48a0a41069d11a412ac3|title=McAdams-Love race in Utah spurred $11M in spending|first=BRADY|last=McCOMBS|date=December 7, 2018|website=AP NEWS|access-date=July 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709051122/https://apnews.com/0ff703c6668a48a0a41069d11a412ac3|archive-date=July 9, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

With his win, McAdams became the first Democratic member of Congress elected from Utah since [[Jim Matheson]] won reelection to the 4th district in 2012.

==== 2020 ====
{{See also|2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 4}}

McAdams was challenged by Republican [[Burgess Owens]], a former [[NFL]] player and frequent contributor on [[Fox News]]. A [[United Utah Party]] candidate, Jonia Broderick, dropped out in October and endorsed McAdams.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fox13now.com/news/election-2020/united-utah-party-candidate-drops-out-of-race-endorses-mcadams|title=United Utah Party candidate drops out of race, endorses McAdams|date=October 14, 2020|publisher=Fox 13 SLC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019060213/https://www.fox13now.com/news/election-2020/united-utah-party-candidate-drops-out-of-race-endorses-mcadams|archive-date=October 19, 2020|access-date=October 19, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Outside groups spent heavily to oppose McAdams.<ref>{{cite news |author=Brown |first=Matthew |date=January 2, 2019 |title=Utah's new Democratic congressman already has a target on his back, and he's not the only one |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900048573/utahs-new-democratic-party-congressman-ben-mcadams-already-has-a-target-on-his-back-washington-dc-trump.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103143905/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900048573/utahs-new-democratic-party-congressman-ben-mcadams-already-has-a-target-on-his-back-washington-dc-trump.html |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> On November 17 the election was called for Burgess Owens, with a margin less than 1%. Owens won the election by overperforming in traditionally Democratic Salt Lake County, and he ultimately defeated McAdams by approximately 3,000 votes, a larger margin than McAdams won by in 2018.<ref name=2020election/> The election was one of the closest House races in the country in 2020, as it was not officially called until thirteen days after Election Day.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/50050055/burgess-owens-wins-back-utahs-4th-congressional-district-seat-for-republicans |title=Burgess Owens wins back Utah's 4th Congressional District seat for Republicans. KSL. November 16, 2020. Accessed September 26, 2024. |access-date=September 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240713102704/https://www.ksl.com/article/50050055/burgess-owens-wins-back-utahs-4th-congressional-district-seat-for-republicans |archive-date=July 13, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==== 2026 ====
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 1}}

After the Third District Judge Dianna Gibson ruled in August 2025 that Utah's current congressional maps were unfairly drawn to favor Republicans and that the maps had to be redrawn by the legislature, McAdams is the new contender for the newly redrawn 1st district, which will be centered around Salt Lake County.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Robert |date=2025-09-05 |title=6 Democratic candidates to watch if Utah redraws its congressional maps |url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2025/09/05/6-democratic-candidates-to-watch-if-utah-redraws-its-congressional-maps/ |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Deseret News |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011042850/https://www.deseret.com/utah/2025/09/05/6-democratic-candidates-to-watch-if-utah-redraws-its-congressional-maps/ |archive-date=October 11, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> McAdams announced his run on November 13.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gehrke |first1=Robert |title=Ben McAdams makes it official — the Democrat is running again for Congress in Utah |url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2025/11/13/ben-mcadams-is-running-utahs-new/ |access-date=November 13, 2025 |work=The Salt Lake Tribune |date=November 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113143916/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2025/11/13/ben-mcadams-is-running-utahs-new/ |archive-date=November 13, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In November 2025, [[Politico]] speculated that the relatively moderate McAdams could struggle in the deep-blue 1st district.<ref>[https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/17/utah-democrats-got-a-gift-now-comes-the-headache-00653575 Utah Democrats got a gift. Now comes the headache. Politico. November 17, 2025.]</ref> However, McAdams was the first to gather the necessary signatures to appear on the primary ballot and led other Democratic candidates in fundraising through the end of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/02/02/utah-democrats-fundraising-report/ |title=Former Rep. Ben McAdams leads the pack in fundraising for Utah's redrawn 1st District. Deseret News. February 13, 2026 |access-date=March 2, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260314171637/https://www.ksl.com/article/51447635/former-rep-ben-mcadams-first-democrat-to-qualify-for-ballot-in-utahs-new-1st-district |archive-date=March 14, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> He also led in polling among the Democratic field through March 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://utahpolitics.news/poll-mcadams-leads-democratic-field-in-1st-district-race/ |title=Poll: McAdams leads Democratic field in Utah's 1st congressional district race. Utah Political Watch. ===Tenure===

McAdams was the only Democrat in Utah's congressional delegation during the 116th Congress.

Following attacks from Mia Love during the 2018 campaign, seeking to tie McAdams to House speaker [[Nancy Pelosi]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/07/26/despite-rep-mia-loves/|title=Utah Democrat insists he's just as anti-abortion as his conservative opponent|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|date=July 27, 2018|access-date=March 15, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181223190504/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/07/26/despite-rep-mia-loves/|archive-date=December 23, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> McAdams voted for [[Stephanie Murphy]], a Democratic representative from [[Florida]], for House speaker.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://kjzz.com/news/local/mcadams-keeps-campaign-promise-votes-against-pelosi-as-speaker-of-the-house|title=McAdams keeps campaign promise, votes against Pelosi as Speaker of the House|author=Larry D. Curtis|date=January 3, 2019|publisher=KUTV|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190106104409/https://kjzz.com/news/local/mcadams-keeps-campaign-promise-votes-against-pelosi-as-speaker-of-the-house|archive-date=January 6, 2019|access-date=January 5, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/01/03/ben-mcadams-sworn-new-us/|title=Ben McAdams sworn in as new U.S. House member. Utah's only Democrat in Congress casts his first vote against Pelosi as speaker|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=January 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190203004924/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/01/03/ben-mcadams-sworn-new-us/|archive-date=February 3, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

McAdams was one of over 100 members of Congress who asked to have their pay withheld during the [[2018–19 United States federal government shutdown]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/01/08/politics/congress-members-no-pay-shutdown/index.html|title=More than 100 members of Congress reject pay during shutdown|access-date=January 19, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114210552/https://www.cnn.com/2019/01/08/politics/congress-members-no-pay-shutdown/index.html|archive-date=January 14, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2019, McAdams introduced legislation proposing a [[Balanced Budget Amendment]] to the [[U.S. Constitution]]. He was supported by the other 26 members of the Blue Dog Caucus. The amendment would have allowed deficits during wars, recessions, or sustained periods of high unemployment. It would have also protected [[Social Security (United States)|Social Security]] and [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] from court-mandated budget cuts. As justification for the amendment, McAdams cited the $22 trillion debt, $1 trillion annual deficit, increasing interest payments, and lack of efforts by either party to curtail spending growth.<ref>{{cite news|title=Moderate Democrats Back Balanced-Budget Amendment, Countering Liberals|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-04-09/moderate-democrats-back-balanced-budget-countering-liberals|publisher=Bloomberg|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410161047/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-04-09/moderate-democrats-back-balanced-budget-countering-liberals|archive-date=April 10, 2019|access-date=April 10, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Burr |first=Thomas |date=April 9, 2019 |title=Normally a Republican idea, Utah's Democratic Rep. Ben McAdams proposes a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution |url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/04/09/democratic-rep-ben/ |publisher=Salt Lake Tribune |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410161049/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/04/09/democratic-rep-ben/ |archive-date=April 10, 2019 |access-date=April 10, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |title=Utah Rep. Ben McAdams proposes balanced budget amendment, says deficit is 'bipartisan problem' |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900065002/utah-rep-ben-mcadams-balanced-budget-constitution-amendment-deficit-bipartisan.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410161046/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900065002/utah-rep-ben-mcadams-balanced-budget-constitution-amendment-deficit-bipartisan.html |archive-date=April 10, 2019 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://utahpolicy.com/index.php/features/today-at-utah-policy/20054-mcadams-introduces-balanced-budget-amendment|title=McAdams introduces Balanced Budget Amendment|publisher=Utah Policy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410161050/https://utahpolicy.com/index.php/features/today-at-utah-policy/20054-mcadams-introduces-balanced-budget-amendment|archive-date=April 10, 2019|access-date=April 10, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Liberal-leaning news sources criticized the plan.<ref>{{Cite 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://splinternews.com/the-worst-democrats-in-congress-want-to-make-the-worst-1833920154|title=The Worst Democrats in Congress Want a Balanced Budget 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410161049/https://splinternews.com/the-worst-democrats-in-congress-want-to-make-the-worst-1833920154|archive-date=April 10, 2019|url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2019/apr/10/fiscally-conservative-democrats-green-new-deal|title=Fiscally-conservative Democrats have declared war on the Green New Deal|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

McAdams introduced a bill to help victims of [[Ponzi schemes]] recover their money. On November 18, 2019, it passed the House of Representatives with bipartisan support. Utah has the highest number of known Ponzi schemes per capita in the United States.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldextra.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/u-s-house-passes-rep-ben-mcadams-bill-that-would/article_7158ad66-773c-5cf8-a2fc-5cf5d394d371.amp.html|title=U.S. House passes Rep. Ben McAdams' bill that would help Ponzi scheme victims recover funds|publisher=Daily Herald|access-date=November 26, 2019|archive-date=November 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191127210134/https://www.heraldextra.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/u-s-house-passes-rep-ben-mcadams-bill-that-would/article_7158ad66-773c-5cf8-a2fc-5cf5d394d371.amp.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

McAdams introduced an amendment to a funding bill to prevent resumption of [[nuclear weapons testing]], which passed the House in July 2019.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/07/20/house-passes-ben-mcadams/|title=House passes Ben McAdams' ban on nuclear weapons testing|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|date=July 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019134241/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/07/20/house-passes-ben-mcadams/|archive-date=October 19, 2020|access-date=October 19, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Political positions ==
Ahead of 2018 and 2020 elections, McAdams described himself as a [[moderate Democrat]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wtop.com/national/2018/04/utah-democrats-gather-to-select-congressional-nominees/|title=Utah Democrats nominate McAdams for House race against Love {{!}} WTOP|date=April 28, 2018|work=WTOP|access-date=August 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810205625/https://wtop.com/national/2018/04/utah-democrats-gather-to-select-congressional-nominees/|archive-date=August 10, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/46310286/mcadams-wilson-easily-win-nominations-at-democratic-state-convention|title=McAdams, Wilson, easily win nominations at Democratic state convention|access-date=August 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129071354/https://www.ksl.com/article/46310286/mcadams-wilson-easily-win-nominations-at-democratic-state-convention|archive-date=January 29, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He emphasized his efforts to work with Republicans, and said he believed it is important to work together to solve problems.<ref name="WrongToTalk">{{cite news|url=https://utahpolicy.com/index.php/features/today-at-utah-policy/18947-mcadams-says-democrats-are-wrong-to-talk-about-impeaching-president-trump|title=McAdams says Democrats are wrong to talk about impeaching President Trump|publisher=Utahpolicy.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190104234412/https://utahpolicy.com/index.php/features/today-at-utah-policy/18947-mcadams-says-democrats-are-wrong-to-talk-about-impeaching-president-trump|archive-date=January 4, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Utah Rep. Ben McAdams still finds optimism in Washington after a polarizing first year|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/01/01/after-polarizing-first/|date=January 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920121341/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/01/01/after-polarizing-first/|archive-date=September 20, 2020|access-date=August 3, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Rep.-elect Ben McAdams says he wants to get to work on DACA, could vote for a Republican speaker over Nancy Pelosi|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/11/23/rep-elect-ben-mcadams/|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|date=November 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929031732/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/11/23/rep-elect-ben-mcadams/|archive-date=September 29, 2020|access-date=August 3, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Politico]], however, described McAdams as a [[conservative Democrat]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-29 |title=Democrats zero in on a red state in the redistricting battle |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/29/democrats-seize-on-utah-in-redistricting-war-00535242 |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=POLITICO |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251102061136/https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/29/democrats-seize-on-utah-in-redistricting-war-00535242 |archive-date=November 2, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> and according to the [[UCLA]] Department of Political Science's [[NOMINATE (scaling method)|DW-NOMINATE]] scores, McAdams was the most conservative Democrat in the 116th House.<ref>As of July 2020. {{cite web|url=https://voteview.com/person/21943/ben-mcadams|title=Voteview – McADAMS, Ben|publisher=voteview.com, UCLA Department of Political Science|access-date=July 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818171133/https://voteview.com/person/21943/ben-mcadams|archive-date=August 18, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ahead of the 2026 election, Utah Governor Cox stated that McAdams had taken positions further to the left as a result of the redistricting.<ref name = "Mamdani">{{Cite web|title='From moderate to Mamdani-land': Gov. Cox says Utah redistricting ruling created 'extreme' congressional districts|url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/11/25/utah-governor-criticizes-redistricting-ruling-for-making-extreme-districts-with-bad-political-incentives/|website=Deseret News|date=2025-11-26|access-date=2025-12-02|language=en|last=Tomco|first=Brigham|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251126194047/https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/11/25/utah-governor-criticizes-redistricting-ruling-for-making-extreme-districts-with-bad-political-incentives/|archive-date=November 26, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Utah's last Democrat in Congress, Ben McAdams, is running again in 2026 • Utah News Dispatch|url=https://utahnewsdispatch.com/2025/11/13/utah-last-democrat-in-congress-ben-mcadams-running-2026/|website=Utah News Dispatch|date=2025-11-13|access-date=2025-12-02|language=en-US|first=Katie|last=McKellar|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118190855/https://utahnewsdispatch.com/2025/11/13/utah-last-democrat-in-congress-ben-mcadams-running-2026/|archive-date=November 18, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> In announcing his run, however, McAdams noted "I haven't changed. People know that I'll work with anyone to get results," and urged the Democratic Party to be more inclusive of diverse viewpoints.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Ben McAdams pushes for inclusive Democratic Party as he launches comeback bid|url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/11/13/ben-mcadams-launches-comeback-house-bid/|website=Deseret News|date=2025-11-13|access-date=2026-03-15|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251129075323/https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/11/13/ben-mcadams-launches-comeback-house-bid/|archive-date=November 29, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Abortion===
As a Utah state senator, McAdams opposed a bill to increase the waiting period for abortions from 24 to 72 hours, a bill mandating biannual inspections of abortion clinics, a bill requiring doctors to describe ultrasound images to patients, and a bill that would have allowed health care providers to refuse to perform abortions on religious grounds. As such, he received a 100% rating from the pro-choice [[Planned Parenthood]] Action Council of Utah for his time as a state senator (2011-2012).<ref name=":3" /> In 2018, however, under fire from Love's campaign, he said he voted against the anti-abortion bills because he considered them poorly written and was concerned about their unintended legal consequences, not because he supported abortion.<ref name="AntiAbortion">{{Cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/07/26/despite-rep-mia-loves/|title=Utah Democrat insists he's just as anti-abortion as his conservative opponent|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=August 10, 2018|author=Connor Richards|date=July 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181223190504/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/07/26/despite-rep-mia-loves/|archive-date=December 23, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Rewire7312018">{{cite web |url=https://rewire.news/article/2018/07/31/utah-democrats-abortion-stance-sparks-questions-ahead-of-midterms/ |title=Utah Democrat's Abortion Stance Sparks Questions Ahead of Midterms |last=Knight |first=Nicole |date=July 31, 2018 |publisher=Rewire News |access-date=September 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190928194832/https://rewire.news/article/2018/07/31/utah-democrats-abortion-stance-sparks-questions-ahead-of-midterms/ |archive-date=September 28, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

During the 2018 election campaign, McAdams described himself as pro-life, referring to his "deeply held beliefs about the sanctity of life", and said that Mia Love's charge that he is an abortion advocate was "offensive". McAdams also said "decisions about terminating a pregnancy should [be] made by a woman in consultation with her physician, family members, and faith counselors she trusts".<ref name = "AntiAbortion" /> 

During the 2026 election campaign, McAdams has pledged support for abortion rights<ref name = "NewsHour">{{Cite web |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrats-try-new-tactic-to-win-a-house-seat-in-utah-running-as-progressives-in-a-red-state |title=Democrats try new tactic to win a House seat in Utah — running as progressives in a red state. PBS NewsHour. March 31, 2026. |website=[[PBS]] |date=March 31, 2026 |access-date=April 6, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260402084319/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrats-try-new-tactic-to-win-a-house-seat-in-utah-running-as-progressives-in-a-red-state |archive-date=April 2, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>, referring to them as “health care,” and saying he would vote to “codify [[Roe v. Wade|Roe]] and restore a woman’s right to choose” if elected.<ref name = "Mamdani" />

===Economic issues===

McAdams opposed the [[Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017]] because of the expected $1.5 trillion increase of the national debt over 10 years. He also said it favors the "wealthy over the middle class".<ref name="DeseretNewsToneOfRace"/> He has stated he believes in tax code modernization, but that he considered the tax reform bill "fiscally irresponsible", and believes that its cost "is borrowed from future generations".<ref name="DeseretNewsToneOfRace" />

McAdams supported measures to reduce the federal deficit, including a [[Balanced Budget Amendment]] to the US Constitution.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/2019/3/11/20667988/ben-mcadams-both-parties-must-work-to-lower-our-country-s-dangerous-debt-burden/|title=Ben McAdams: Both parties must work to lower our country's dangerous debt burden|publisher=Deseret News|date=March 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812015359/https://www.deseret.com/2019/3/11/20667988/ben-mcadams-both-parties-must-work-to-lower-our-country-s-dangerous-debt-burden/|archive-date=August 12, 2025|access-date=November 7, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2019, McAdams voted against a House bill to increase the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour. He said he supported a higher minimum wage, but wanted a system that sets the rate based on the regional cost of living and purchasing power.<ref>{{cite news |last=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |date=July 18, 2019 |title=Democrat Ben McAdams, rest of Utah delegation, vote against $15 federal minimum wage |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900080206/minimum-wage-utah-delegation-ben-mcadams-chris-stewart-rob-bishop-john-curtis.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190718200034/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900080206/minimum-wage-utah-delegation-ben-mcadams-chris-stewart-rob-bishop-john-curtis.html |archive-date=July 18, 2019 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> Ahead of the 2026 election, during a forum for young voters, McAdams pledged to support a minimum wage increase.<ref name = "NewsHour" />

McAdams was one of 18 Democrats who opposed a $2.2 trillion [[COVID-19]] relief stimulus bill sponsored by Democrats. McAdams said the bill was "a step in the right direction [for economic relief from COVID] but [was] still weighted down with partisan wish list items unrelated to the COVID crisis".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/10/02/ben-mcadams-bucks-party|title=Ben McAdams bucks party on COVID-19 relief bill, as GOP ads complain he follows Dems in lockstep|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=February 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227180911/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/10/02/ben-mcadams-bucks-party/|archive-date=February 27, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Energy and environment===

McAdams supports efforts to improve Utah's air quality. He requested that the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee double the funding available for the [[Utah Transit Authority]] to purchase electric buses, in an effort to improve air quality.<ref>{{cite news |author=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |date=May 31, 2019 |title=UTA, Utah Rep. Ben McAdams working to secure more federal dollars for electric buses |url=https://www.deseret.com/2019/5/31/20674644/uta-utah-rep-ben-mcadams-working-to-secure-more-federal-dollars-for-electric-buses/ |publisher=Deseret News |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812015418/https://www.deseret.com/2019/5/31/20674644/uta-utah-rep-ben-mcadams-working-to-secure-more-federal-dollars-for-electric-buses/ |archive-date=August 12, 2025 |access-date=November 7, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Together with Representative [[John Curtis]], McAdams introduced legislation that would make projects like [[FrontRunner]] eligible for federal funding.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2020/2/14/21137966/ben-macadams-john-curtis-utah-transit-authority-frontrunner-federal-transportation-train|title=McAdams, Curtis aim to secure federal money for FrontRunner double-tracking|first=Dennis|last=Romboy|date=February 14, 2020|website=Deseret News|access-date=February 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200303031639/https://www.deseret.com/utah/2020/2/14/21137966/ben-macadams-john-curtis-utah-transit-authority-frontrunner-federal-transportation-train|archive-date=March 3, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

McAdams voted for a bill to block the Trump administration from leaving the [[Paris Agreement]]. He was the only member of the Utah congressional delegation to do so.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/46543866/rep-ben-mcadams-casts-lone-utah-vote-to-block-trump-withdrawal-from-paris-climate-accord|publisher=KSL|title=Rep. Ben McAdams casts lone Utah vote to block Trump withdrawal from Paris climate accord|date=May 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530035709/https://www.ksl.com/article/46543866/rep-ben-mcadams-casts-lone-utah-vote-to-block-trump-withdrawal-from-paris-climate-accord|archive-date=May 30, 2019|access-date=May 30, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> In August 2019, McAdams called climate change "the greatest challenge of our time", calling for bipartisan efforts to address it and for Utah to be a leader in those efforts.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/opinion/commentary/2019/08/24/ben-mcadams-what-world/|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|title=Ben McAdams: What the world will see in Utah on responding to climate change|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191118030913/https://www.sltrib.com/opinion/commentary/2019/08/24/ben-mcadams-what-world/|archive-date=November 18, 2019|access-date=December 1, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> On the other hand, McAdams did not support the [[Green New Deal]] in 2019; he said he would have preferred "government working hand-in-hand with the private sector" to harness "the creativity and entrepreneurship of the private sector... to solve [the] crisis" of climate change. McAdams believes in "the threat of climate change", which he says is "real... and we are seeing it... in Utah".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kutv.com/news/connect-to-congress/mcadams-connect-to-congress-no-deal-on-the-green-new-deal|title=McAdams Connect To Congress: No deal on the Green New Deal|first=Heidi|last=Hatch|date=March 27, 2019|website=KUTV|access-date=July 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329183805/https://kutv.com/news/connect-to-congress/mcadams-connect-to-congress-no-deal-on-the-green-new-deal|archive-date=March 29, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Gun policy ===
In 2019, McAdams said that he supports the [[Second Amendment to the United States Constitution|Second Amendment]] but believes in more responsible gun ownership laws.<ref name="Deseret932019">{{cite web |url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2019/9/3/20847892/utah-representative-ben-mcadams-gun-violence-universal-background-checks |title=Rep. Ben McAdams on guns: 'I want to consider any option that will save the lives of our kids' |last=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |date=September 3, 2019 |publisher=Deseret News |access-date=November 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191104170257/https://www.deseret.com/utah/2019/9/3/20847892/utah-representative-ben-mcadams-gun-violence-universal-background-checks |archive-date=November 4, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2019, McAdams voted for a bill requiring background checks for all gun buyers. All of Utah's other representatives voted against it. At the same time, he voted for a Republican-backed amendment requiring [[Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] to be notified when an illegal immigrant attempts to buy a firearm and is caught during the background check.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/02/27/utah-rep-ben-mcadams/|title=Utah Rep. Ben McAdams supports universal background checks for gun buyers. Utah's Republican members all vote no.|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=March 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190228115241/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/02/27/utah-rep-ben-mcadams/|archive-date=February 28, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/02/28/mcadams-backed-expanding/|title=McAdams backed expanding background checks for guns — but opposed extending wait periods|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=March 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301130750/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/02/28/mcadams-backed-expanding/|archive-date=March 1, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Healthcare===

While Salt Lake County mayor, McAdams, called for Congress to make fixes to the [[Affordable Care Act]] (or Obamacare) instead of repealing it.<ref name="DeseretNewsToneOfRace">{{cite news |author=Roche |first=Lisa Riley |date=October 14, 2018 |title=Ben McAdams: Democratic challenger disappointed with tone of race |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900036945/ben-mcadams-democratic-challenger-disappointed-with-tone-of-race.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181015112651/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900036945/ben-mcadams-democratic-challenger-disappointed-with-tone-of-race.html |archive-date=October 15, 2018 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> He had previously called on Congress to renew the [[Children’s Health Insurance Program|Children's Health Insurance Program]] (CHIP) after its funding lapsed in September 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/opinion/commentary/2017/12/02/ben-mcadams-congress-to-tiny-tim-no-health-insurance-for-you/|title=Ben McAdams: Congress to Tiny Tim: 'No health insurance for you.'|author=Ben McAdams|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=October 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404003525/https://www.sltrib.com/opinion/commentary/2017/12/02/ben-mcadams-congress-to-tiny-tim-no-health-insurance-for-you/|archive-date=April 4, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>  McAdams did not support a "[[Medicare for All Act|Medicare-for-all]]" type plan in 2019, because he said it would not "work for [his] constituents".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schott|first=Bryan|date=March 31, 2019|title=McAdams on Medicare for all: 'Not an approach to healthcare that works for my constituents'|url=https://www.utahpolicy.com/index.php/features/today-at-utah-policy/19944-mcadams-on-medicare-for-all-not-an-approach-to-healthcare-that-works-for-my-constituents|website=utahpolicy.com|access-date=April 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401181954/https://www.utahpolicy.com/index.php/features/today-at-utah-policy/19944-mcadams-on-medicare-for-all-not-an-approach-to-healthcare-that-works-for-my-constituents|archive-date=April 1, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Immigration===

McAdams has called for comprehensive immigration reform that includes secured borders, increased legal immigration, and a permanent solution for participants in the [[Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals]] (DACA) program, also known as Dreamers.<ref name="DeseretNewsToneOfRace"/> He also supports the principles in the [[Utah Compact]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/opinion/commentary/2019/03/30/ben-mcadams-derek-miller/|title=Ben McAdams and Derek Miller: A new generation of leaders stands for the principles of the Utah Compact|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401182111/https://www.sltrib.com/opinion/commentary/2019/03/30/ben-mcadams-derek-miller/|archive-date=April 1, 2019|access-date=April 1, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

During the 2018 election campaign, McAdams opposed President Trump's plans to build a wall on the southern U.S. border with [[Mexico]].<ref name="BeyondTheAttackAds">{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/10/28/beyond-attack-ads-here/|title=Beyond the attack ads: Here are the candidates' stands on issues in the Mia Love vs. Ben McAdams race|date=October 28, 2018|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404003823/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2018/10/28/beyond-attack-ads-here/|archive-date=April 4, 2019|access-date=December 21, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> During the 2018–19 government shutdown, McAdams said he could accept additional border protection funding, potentially including a wall, if it were part of a compromise bill that included immigration reform and "a fix for the Dreamers and DACA". The government shutdown centered on Trump's demands for additional funds to construct a wall and the unwillingness of House Democrats to agree to it.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://kutv.com/news/local/mcadams-says-border-wall-is-not-immoral-could-vote-for-it-under-certain-circumstances|title=McAdams says border wall is not immoral, could vote for it under certain circumstances|publisher=KUTV|date=January 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122044011/https://kutv.com/news/local/mcadams-says-border-wall-is-not-immoral-could-vote-for-it-under-certain-circumstances|archive-date=January 22, 2019|access-date=January 21, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

McAdams pushed back against a Trump administration plan to rescind visas for immediate family members of [[H-1B visa|H-1B]] legal immigrants. H-1B visa holders are skilled workers who immigrate with company sponsorship. [[H-4 visa]]s, which the plan would affect, are issued to their spouses and children under 21.<ref>{{cite news |last=Raymond |first=Art |title=Rep. Ben McAdams pushing back on Trump plan to cut visas for spouses of tech workers |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900067351/utah-rep-ben-mcadams-president-donald-trump-plan-to-cut-h-1b-visas-spouses-tech-workers.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424042629/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900067351/utah-rep-ben-mcadams-president-donald-trump-plan-to-cut-h-1b-visas-spouses-tech-workers.html |archive-date=April 24, 2019 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref>

===LGBTQ rights===

McAdams supports [[same-sex marriage]]. After the Supreme Court ruled in ''[[Obergefell v. Hodges]]'' that same-sex couples have the right to marry, McAdams stated: "As [[Anthony Kennedy|Justice Kennedy]] stated in his opinion, 'The right of same-sex couples to marry is derived from the [[Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Fourteenth Amendment]]'s guarantee of equal protection.' This decision enshrines what I've long believed—that all families should be treated equally under the law".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc4.com/news/mayor-ben-mcadams-pleased-with-supreme-court-same-sex-marriage-ruling/|title=Mayor Ben McAdams 'pleased' with Supreme Court same-sex marriage ruling|date=June 26, 2015|work=GOOD4UTAH|access-date=August 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220518130435/https://www.abc4.com/news/mayor-ben-mcadams-pleased-with-supreme-court-same-sex-marriage-ruling/|archive-date=May 18, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2019, McAdams voted for the [[Equality Act (United States)|Equality Act]],<ref>{{cite news|series=House Debate on the Equality Act|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/05/17/mcadams-joins-democrats/|title=Rep. Ben McAdams joins Democrats in passing Equality Act; other Utahns in Congress vote no|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune|date=May 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629162548/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/05/17/mcadams-joins-democrats/|archive-date=June 29, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> which would legally prohibit [[discrimination]] on the basis of [[sexual orientation]] and [[gender identity]] in [[employment]], [[housing]], [[public accommodations]], [[public education]], [[federal funding]], [[credit (finance)|credit]], and the [[jury system]]. Despite his vote, McAdams has stated he "do[es]n't think it's perfect" and supports continued dialogue and refinement of the bill.<ref>{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Matthew |title=Why Utah Congressman Ben McAdams says he's 'uniquely situated' to bridge Equality Act, religious liberties |url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2019/9/7/20849448/utah-ben-mcadams-equality-act-religious-freedom-lgbtq-nondiscrimination-student-housing |publisher=Deseret News |publication-date=2019-09-07 |df=mdy |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909030544/https://www.deseret.com/utah/2019/9/7/20849448/utah-ben-mcadams-equality-act-religious-freedom-lgbtq-nondiscrimination-student-housing |archive-date=September 9, 2019 |access-date=September 9, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Trump administrations===
====First Trump administration====
After the [[Trump–Ukraine scandal#Release and substance of the complaint|whistleblower complaint]] in the [[Trump–Ukraine scandal]] was released to the public, McAdams expressed support for [[Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump|an impeachment inquiry]]. He said an inquiry was necessary because Trump had "refus[ed] to further cooperate with congressional oversight, without an impeachment inquiry".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/10/04/rep-ben-mcadams-says/|title='I am not on the fence': Ben McAdams throws his support behind Trump impeachment inquiry|publisher=Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref> On December 18, 2019, McAdams voted for both articles of impeachment against Trump.<ref>Grace Panetta [https://www.businessinsider.com/trump-impeachment-vote-results-house-2019-12 WHIP COUNT: Here's which members of the House voted for and against impeaching Trump] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191224170114/https://www.businessinsider.com/trump-impeachment-vote-results-house-2019-12 |date=December 24, 2019 }} Dec 18, 2019 businessinsider.com</ref> Two days earlier, he had announced his intention to vote for impeachment, saying, "for me, the evidence is clear" that Trump attempted to undermine the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]] by soliciting aid from Ukraine to help his own reelection efforts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2019/12/16/ben-mcadams-vote-to-impeach-trump-086215 |title=Vulnerable Democrats to vote to impeach Trump |last=Ferris |first=Sarah |date=December 16, 2019 |publisher=Politico |access-date=December 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217025427/https://www.politico.com/news/2019/12/16/ben-mcadams-vote-to-impeach-trump-086215 |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====Second Trump administration====
In announcing his 2026 campaign, McAdams accused Trump of "trampling" on "democracy and our Constitution," and faulted the administration for failing to handle problems with inflation and affordability.<ref name=":2" />

==Personal life==
McAdams is one of six children.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://benmcadamsforcongress.com/about/|title=Meet Ben McAdams|access-date=August 11, 2018|archive-date=November 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116090628/https://benmcadamsforcongress.com/about/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a member of [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] (LDS Church),<ref name="McAdamsProfile Deseret"/> and served a [[Mission (LDS Church)|mission]] to [[Brazil]] in the mid-1990s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ozy.com/politics-and-power/theres-a-reason-hes-the-highest-ranking-dem-in-utah/75784|title=There's a Reason He's the Highest-Ranking Dem in Utah|first=Libby|last=Coleman|website=OZY|date=February 20, 2017|access-date=July 9, 2019|archive-date=July 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709051134/https://www.ozy.com/politics-and-power/theres-a-reason-hes-the-highest-ranking-dem-in-utah/75784|url-status=dead}}</ref> McAdams and his wife, Julie, have four children.<ref name="McAdamsProfile Deseret"/>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], McAdams announced he had tested positive for [[COVID-19]] on March 18, 2020. He was the second sitting member of Congress to test positive, after [[Mario Díaz-Balart]] earlier that day.<ref>{{cite web |title=BREAKING: Ben McAdams tests positive for #COVID19 |url=https://twitter.com/KUTV2News/status/1240435212682588161 |website=KUTV 2News |access-date=March 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326023637/https://twitter.com/KUTV2News/status/1240435212682588161 |archive-date=March 26, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/03/24/sen-mitt-romney-tests/|title=Sen. Mitt Romney tests negative for COVID-19; Rep. Ben McAdams remains hospitalized.|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327210902/https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/03/24/sen-mitt-romney-tests/|archive-date=March 27, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> On March 22, McAdams announced that he had been hospitalized since March 20 due to a "severe shortness of breath" related to [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1241878967327559680|user=BenMcAdamsUT|title=Thank you everyone for your well...|date=March 23, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://time.com/5808196/congressman-ben-mcadams-coronavirus/|title=Congressman Ben McAdams Hospitalized With 'Severe Shortness of Breath' From COVID-19|first=Billy|last=Perrigo|publisher=Time|date=March 22, 2020|access-date=March 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324224659/https://time.com/5808196/congressman-ben-mcadams-coronavirus/|archive-date=March 24, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> He was released from the hospital on March 28.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/46735839/utah-rep-ben-mcadams-released-from-hospital|title=Utah Rep. Ben McAdams released from hospital|website=www.ksl.com|access-date=February 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927013143/https://www.ksl.com/article/46735839/utah-rep-ben-mcadams-released-from-hospital|archive-date=September 27, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>
